title: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
capsule: The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies was formally constituted in 1816 by Ferdinand I, who merged the Kingdom of Naples and Kingdom of Sicily into a single Bourbon realm after the Napoleonic interlude. It was the largest and most populous state on the Italian peninsula, encompassing southern Italy from the Papal States border to Sicily, but was characterized by agrarian underdevelopment and authoritarian governance that made it a target of liberal nationalist criticism. Giuseppe Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand landed in Sicily in May 1860 and swept northward; the last Bourbon king Francesco II surrendered, and the kingdom was formally annexed into the newly proclaimed Kingdom of Italy in 1861.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders are precisely established from early-nineteenth-century cartography and treaty records; the island of Sicily and peninsular boundaries with the Papal States are well documented.
